title: How do you design tamper-evident audit logs using Merkle trees and hashing?
snippet: Tamper-evident audit logs use an approach where each entry is protected with cryptographic hashing so that any change or deletion can be detected later. Hash chaining requires scanning the entire prefix of the log for verification, while Merkle trees improve this by allowing proofs of inclusion.
claim: Hash chains protect audit entries cryptographically but require full-prefix scans; Merkle trees enable logarithmic inclusion proofs.

title: Mastering Event Sourcing: A Pattern for Scalable, Auditable Systems
snippet: A snapshot is a periodic checkpoint of the aggregate's current state, stored alongside the event stream. Instead of replaying all 50,000 events, the system loads the snapshot at event 49,500 and replays only the 500 events that came after. Projections or read models are used to make reading data more efficient.
claim: Event sourcing uses snapshots at periodic boundaries to skip replaying long event prefixes, with projections optimizing read-side queries.
